title: Titans GM Mike Borgonzi Denies Jeffery Simmons Trade Plans After Late Bears Call, NBC Sports Reports
body:
The Tennessee Titans’ front office confirmed that the franchise never intended to move defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, even as the Chicago Bears reportedly reached out last night to discuss a potential trade. General manager Mike Borgonzi told reporters that the organization’s long‑term plan still revolves around keeping Simmons as a cornerstone of the defensive line, and that any speculation about a deal was purely the product of rumor‑monger chatter rather than a concrete strategy.

Simmons, who entered the 2026 season without any indication that a trade was looming, addressed the media on Wednesday afternoon. He reiterated that he had not heard any official word about a move and emphasized his commitment to the Titans. “I’m focused on the team, the game plan, and doing my part,” Simmons said, adding that the NFL’s business side can shift quickly, but he remains confident in the organization’s direction. His comments came as the Titans’ defensive line continued to rank among the league’s most productive units, a status that has made Simmons a valuable asset both on the field and in the trade market.

Borgonzi’s remarks provide a clearer picture of the Titans’ strategic calculus. The team, still reeling from a disappointing 2025 campaign that saw them miss the playoffs, has been actively reshaping its roster while trying to maintain continuity on defense. “We never set out to trade Jeffery,” Borgonzo said. “Our focus is on building a competitive team around him, and any discussions that have taken place are exploratory at best.” The GM’s comments also suggest that the Bears’ outreach was likely a preliminary inquiry rather than a formal proposal, reflecting the NFL’s off‑season habit of testing the waters before committing to major transactions.

Analysts note that the Titans’ reluctance to part with Simmons makes sense given his impact. Since being drafted in 2022, Simmons has recorded double‑digit sack totals in each of his first three seasons and has become a disruptive force against both the run and pass. His presence anchors a defensive front that has helped the Titans keep opponents’ rushing yards per game in the bottom third of the league. Trading him would not only weaken the defense but also send a signal that the franchise is willing to dismantle core pieces for short‑term gains.

On the other side of the equation, Chicago’s interest underscores the Bears’ urgent need to bolster a defensive line that has struggled with injuries and inconsistent play. The Bears have been active in the trade market, seeking to add a proven interior rusher who can immediately elevate their pass rush. While Simmons would be a premium acquisition, the Bears would likely need to part with a combination of draft capital and a young defensive prospect to meet Tennessee’s valuation. The Titans, however, appear to be weighing the long‑term cost of losing a player who still has several prime years ahead against the potential short‑term benefit of additional picks.

The situation also highlights a broader trend in the league where teams are increasingly cautious about moving young, high‑impact defensive players. With the salary‑cap environment tightening and the premium placed on defensive versatility, franchises are more likely to retain talent unless a clear, advantageous return materializes. For the Titans, retaining Simmons aligns with a strategy that emphasizes defensive stability while they continue to fine‑tune the offensive side of the ball under new coaching leadership.

Looking ahead, the next few weeks will be critical for both organizations. The Titans are expected to finalize their free‑agency signings and draft strategy at the upcoming NFL Combine, while the Bears will continue to explore trade options to address their defensive deficiencies. If Simmons remains in Tennessee, the Titans will head into the 2026 season with one of the league’s most formidable interior lines, giving them a solid foundation to compete for a playoff berth. Conversely, should the Bears manage to pull off a deal, it could reshape the defensive landscape for both teams and set a precedent for future high‑profile trades in the league.
